_doc: STT parity ground-truth references for the macOS Metal parity eval
(judge `mac-v1-parity-whisper-metal`, bead mb-mac-v1.6.2, Phase 5).
Each `clips` entry pins a committed audio fixture (under
src-tauri/tests/fixtures/audio/) to its HUMAN ground-truth transcript.
WER/CER are computed against `reference` after normalization
(lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace) -- so `reference`
may be written with natural casing/punctuation for readability.
CORPUS NOTE (honest): only `jfk.wav` is real speech. It is
whisper.cpp's canonical sample -- the closing line of JFK's 1961
inaugural address. The other committed fixtures (silent.wav,
sine_440.wav, mixed.wav) are SYNTHETIC non-speech (see
src/dev_bins/generate_fixtures.rs: zeros / a 440 Hz tone) with no
speech content, so they carry no ground-truth transcript and are
excluded from the WER/CER acceptance (a non-empty transcript over pure
silence is a benign Whisper hallucination, not a parity signal). To
widen this corpus, add TTS-rendered speech fixtures (a Helios task,
per docs/phases/phase2-wave2-brief.md) with their reference text here.
`budget` is the parity acceptance bar (see rationale in the shim
src/dev_bins/mac_whisper_parity_smoke.rs and the module docs of
src/stt/parity_macos_v1.rs). large-v3-turbo-q5 on a clean clip like
jfk.wav is expected to be at or near WER 0; the budget leaves a few %
of slack for q5 quantization + Metal-vs-CUDA numeric drift.

clips.source: whisper.cpp canonical sample; JFK 1961 inaugural address closing line
clips.reference: And so, my fellow Americans: ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country.
